title: When the Yearbook Wakes
premise: Isandro Iversen, a scholarship student who has spent ten years hiding their nonbinary identity and their family's debt, transfers to Hollowmere Academy, a school built over the ruins of an old sanatorium. When a group chat called The Yearbook begins posting predictions that come true with eerie precision, Isandro and four classmates realize the chat is fed by something buried beneath the school that trades futures for memories. To escape, they must win the hollow championship the school worships — and the real one: agreeing on who they are to each other before the entity erases one of them. In the end, Isandro sacrifices their own recorded future to save the group, waking the yearbook's true purpose — remembrance — and walks out changed, seen for the first time.
about_author: Theo Delacroix is the pen name of a former boarding-school archivist who spent years cataloguing student memorabilia no one ever claimed. They write stories about teenagers who refuse to be forgotten.

chapters.title: The New Kid's Careful Heart
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Arriving at Hollowmere Academy mid-year, Isandro navigates orientation while carefully concealing their identity, their scholarship, and their fear of being truly known. A tour guide mentions the school was built over a sanatorium and that old records were never recovered. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened by vigilance; Isandro chooses invisibility as safety.

chapters.title: Five Names in a Group Chat
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. An unknown number adds Isandro to a group chat with four strangers: golden-boy captain Rafe, anxious photographer June, skeptic coder Priya, and quiet legacy student Marcus. The first message predicts a pipe burst in the west wing — which happens within hours. Emotional beat: uneasy fascination; the five bond over shared dread.

chapters.title: Predictions Come Due
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between June and Priya. More predictions land: a fire drill, a failed exam, a broken engagement ring. Each comes true exactly. Priya traces the messages to an IP address inside the school basement; June photographs a sealed door that appears in none of the blueprints. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear as coincidence dies.

chapters.title: What the Sanatorium Kept
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus reveals his grandmother was a sanatorium patient whose name appears on a 1962 admission ledger but in no discharge record. The five break into the sub-basement and find a wall of blank yearbook pages that fill with handwriting when touched. Emotional beat: grief and inheritance; Marcus realizes the school is built on the unremembered.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Rafe's POV. The entity behind the chat — calling itself the Registrar — offers a bargain: win Founders' Day, the school's beloved academic decathlon, and it will release them. Rafe, whose whole identity is winning, throws himself into preparation while hiding that his own future has already been traded away. Emotional beat: desperate purpose masking terror.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro and Rafe grow close during late-night study sessions, and Isandro almost tells the truth about themselves — then learns the Registrar punishes honesty by taking memories. Duty says stay silent; love says speak. Isandro chooses speech, and the chat immediately posts a new prediction: 'One of you will be forgotten by Friday.' Emotional beat: tender, terrified courage.

chapters.title: Friday Comes Early
chapters.summary: June's POV. June wakes to find her photos of the others blank and her own name missing from every roster. The group realizes the Registrar is collecting June because she documented everything. They confront the Registrar in the sub-basement, where it shows them the price of survival: someone must remain as a record. Emotional beat: betrayal of hope; the cost becomes personal.

chapters.title: Winning Is Losing
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The team wins the decathlon, but the Registrar declares the victory void — the championship that matters was never trophies, but whether any of them would choose each other over themselves. Rafe, offered his traded future back in exchange for abandoning the group, refuses. Emotional beat: climax of integrity; victory redefined at the worst moment.

chapters.title: The Page With My Name
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. To free June and close the ledger, someone must let the yearbook record them completely — past, secrets, and unwritten future. Isandro volunteers, confessing everything aloud: their name, their ten careful years, their love for Rafe. The blank pages drink them in, and the sanatorium's lost patients finally get their names read aloud. Emotional beat: sacrificial self-acceptance; being seen costs everything and gives everything.

chapters.title: When the Yearbook Wakes
chapters.summary: Group POV, epilogue-style. The Registrar, having received what it actually wanted — remembrance — releases them all. June's photos return; the patients' names are engraved in the school lobby. Isandro walks out with no guaranteed future and, for the first time, no need for one written by anyone else. Rafe takes their hand in front of everyone. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; survival without erasure.
